result.title: Speaking the Navigator's Language: Trajectory-Grounded Instruction Translation for Frozen Aerial VLN Agents
result.summary: Aerial vision-and-language navigation (VLN) agents are typically trained on detail-rich, trajectory-aligned commands, whereas users issue short, intent-driven instructions; on a frozen OpenFly navigator, this \emph{instruction gap} drops success rate (SR) from $31.03\%$ to $11.33\%$. To scale translator training, we prompt a language model with human-written style examples to convert original commands into paired, intent-centered Weak commands, which yield $15.27\%$ SR. We introduce the \textbf{Trajectory-Grounded Instruction Translator (TGIT)}, a front-end that keeps the navigator frozen and translates Weak inputs into agent-executable commands by learning from its trajectory outcomes. The resulting Weak-trained translator raises Weak-input SR to $37.93\%$ and transfers zero-shot to real human instructions ($11.33\%{\rightarrow}32.51\%$); it also improves held-out OpenFly ($4.95\%{\rightarrow}20.79\%$) and yields recovery on CityNav and AirVLN.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对空中 VLN 中用户简短意图指令与训练用细粒度指令之间的「指令鸿沟」，提出 TGIT 前端：导航器保持冻结，仅训练一个翻译器把 Weak 指令改写为可执行指令，并以导航轨迹结果作为学习信号，从而大幅提升 Weak 输入与真实人类指令下的成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 主线不直接相关，但「冻结推理/决策核心、用最终轨迹结果监督外层接口适配」这一线索可供核查，可能类比 latent 推理中固定内部状态生成、以任务结果监督 interface 或贡献分配的做法。
